$comment: The structure kit: building parts players assemble rather than model.
The whole reason this set exists is §1: neither model emits a mesh, so a player cannot BUILD a
house in Tessera the way they could in the reference — they assemble one out of authored
parts. Six walls, three doors, three windows, three stairs, three roofs, three floors and
three fences is the smallest kit that composes into a building anyone would recognise as
theirs, and every one of them registers against the same 2:1 dimetric grid.

parts.subject: a plain rendered wall section, one storey, flat unbroken face with a shallow plinth
a lime-plastered wall section, one storey, the plaster crazed and patched, ochre-warm
a fired brick wall section, one storey, courses clearly laid, a soldier course at the head
a timber-framed wall section, one storey, dark exposed frame with pale infill panels
an iron-framed glazing wall section, one storey, small green panes in a riveted grid
a half-height wall section, waist high, with a flat coping stone along the top
a single plank door in its frame, closed, with a strap hinge and a ring handle
a pair of tall double doors in one frame, closed, with a central drop bolt
an arched door in a round-headed stone surround, closed, studded with nails
a square multi-pane casement window with a stone sill and open shutters
a round porthole window in a moulded surround, one pane, leaded
a tall narrow sash window, two lights, with a slim sill and no shutters
a straight external stair of eight stone steps with an open side
a stair turning a quarter at a square landing, timber treads on a stone base
a tight iron spiral stair around a central post, one full turn, open risers
a gable roof section with a pitched slate face and an exposed timber barge board
a flat roof section with a low parapet and a lead-lined gutter at one edge
a pantiled roof section, overlapping curved terracotta tiles, one ridge tile at the top
a floor section of wide timber planks, lying flat, running one way, worn along the joints
a floor section of irregular stone flags, lying flat, mortar worn low between them
a floor section of small glazed tiles in a simple two-colour chequer, lying flat
a run of pointed timber picket fence with two rails, paint flaking
a run of iron railing, plain uprights with spear heads and a top rail
a run of clipped hedge to waist height, dense and squared off
